newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks surge to record high.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks surge to record high.

text.p: *Stocks break through 2700 mark shortly after opening following strong Dow performance. Volume 45.44 million, value A$101.9 million, 512 traded, 220 steady, 202 up, 90 down

Australian stocks surged through the 2,700 barrier to a record high shortly after opening on Friday after a rebound on Wall Street and strong performances by resource and bank stocks the previous day.

At 10.10 a.m. (0010 GMT) the All Ordinaries Index was 11.1 points up from Thursday's record closing high to 2,704.4. Friday's new mark was also 9.4 points higher than the previous all-time high set during trading on Tuesday.
The Dow Jones Index on Thursday snapped a three-day run of dips to pick up 58.53 points and close on 7,777.06, prompting local brokers to predict the All Ordinaries would breach 2,700.
Blue chip miner BHP was again at the forefront of the latest surge, reaching A$20.05 in early trade, its highest point since May 8 last year.
At 10.50 a.m. (0050 GMT), BHP was up 16 cents to A$19.88 and the volume leader after 2.7 million shares were traded.
Property and financial services group Lend Lease Corp also rose sharply, up 55 cents or two percent at A$27.90.
Gold miner Rio Tinto and chemicals group ICI Australia Ltd were both down sharply, Rio dropping 23 cents to A$22.80 and ICI falling 18 cents to A$12.35.
